output.entity_proposed: Climate Finance Unit (CFU) under the Climate Change Commission (CCC)
output.proposal: HB No. 11284, the proposed "Green Financing for Climate Change Act", seeks to establish a Climate Finance Unit (CFU) under the Climate Change Commission as the central coordinating, advisory and technical body for climate finance. It aims to strengthen the mobilization, coordination, tracking and equitable use of climate finance from domestic and international sources, including improved access for local government units.
output.alignment: As a government organization measure, the review should examine how the proposed CFU fits within the existing Climate Change Commission and whether its functions duplicate those of agencies already involved in climate finance, budgeting and investment programming, notably the DOF, DBM and DEPDev, consistent with the intent to streamline agencies and reduce overlapping mandates under the Government Optimization Act (RA No. 12231). Of particular interest to DBM are Section 5 (Powers and Functions of the CFU) and Section 9 (Establishment of Climate Finance Registry), which involve climate budget tagging, expenditure tracking and integration with DBM budgeting systems, and Section 4 (Establishment of the Climate Finance Unit), which designates the CFU as a central gateway for disbursing climate funds. The measure aligns with the Environment, Climate, and Disaster Resilience priority area of the FY 2027 Budget Priorities Framework. No LEDAC Common Legislative Agenda item is identified for this measure.
legislative_history: HB No. 11284 was filed on September 14, 2026 by Representative Eric G. Yap in the 20th Congress.
Its status is Filed; later stages are not reflected in the available records.
No earlier version, counterpart measure, substitute bill or committee report was identified in the material reviewed.

output.salient_features:
HB No. 11284 seeks to establish a Climate Finance Unit (CFU) under the Climate Change Commission (CCC) to serve as the central body for climate finance matters. Its salient features are as follows:
a. Section 4 (Establishment of the Climate Finance Unit) provides that the CFU is created under the CCC as the central coordinating, advisory and technical body for climate finance, acting as the gateway for domestic and international climate funds, including identifying sources, setting spending priorities, disbursing funds and tracking expenditures down to the local level.
b. Section 5 (Powers and Functions of the CFU) provides that the CFU shall formulate a National Climate Finance Strategy, serve as the national designated authority or focal point for international climate funds, coordinate with the DOF, DBM and DEPDev on fiscal policy, climate budget tagging and investment programming, provide accreditation support, and develop innovative financing mechanisms and safeguards.
c. Section 6 (Composition of the CFU) provides that the CFU shall be headed by a Director with five core divisions, and allows the CCC to create additional divisions or units as necessary.
d. Section 7 (Powers and Functions of the CFU Director) provides that the Director shall lead the CFU, mobilize climate finance, represent the Philippines in climate finance engagements, and approve, endorse or recommend climate finance projects and programs.
e. Section 8 (Appointment, Qualifications, Term of Office, Compensation and Benefits of the CFU Director and Personnel) provides that the Director shall be appointed by the President upon the recommendation of the CCC with a rank, salary grade and privileges equivalent to an Executive Director, sets minimum qualifications, and allows the engagement of consultants and technical experts; no specific salary grade is stated.
f. Section 9 (Establishment of Climate Finance Registry) provides for a National Climate Finance Registry that tracks climate finance flows, integrates with DBM budgeting systems and COA audit frameworks, and is publicly accessible.
g. Section 10 (Strengthening Local Government Access to Climate Funds) provides that the CFU shall support LGUs in preparing proposals, establish regional climate finance hubs or help desks, and enable LGU direct access to international climate finance subject to national oversight.
h. Section 11 (Institutional Strengthening of the CCC) provides that the CCC may create plantilla positions for the CFU, hire technical experts and establish partnerships.
i. Section 12 (Appropriations) provides that the funds needed shall be charged against the appropriations of the CCC under the General Appropriations Act.
j. Section 13 (Annual Report) provides that the CFU shall report annually to both Houses of Congress on implementation and on the National Climate Finance Strategy.
k. Section 14 (Implementing Rules and Regulations) provides that the CFU shall issue the implementing rules within ninety days after approval, in consultation with stakeholders.
output.related_measures_policy: HB No. 11284 may be considered alongside RA No. 9729, which created the Climate Change Commission that would host the CFU, and RA No. 10174, which established the People's Survival Fund as a climate finance stream. The measure aligns with the Environment, Climate, and Disaster Resilience priority area of the FY 2027 Budget Priorities Framework. The review should assess whether the CFU functions under Section 4 (Establishment of the Climate Finance Unit) and Section 5 (Powers and Functions of the CFU) duplicate existing mandates of the CCC, DOF, DBM and DEPDev, particularly on climate budget tagging and expenditure tracking; whether the gateway and disbursement role is consistent with existing budget execution processes; and the cost of new plantilla positions under Section 11 (Institutional Strengthening of the CCC), consistent with the streamlining objectives of the Government Optimization Act (RA No. 12231).
